items.difficulty_reason: In the situation of the taut descent statements of the chapter, the lemma asserts that if the target ring B is weakly pre-adic then so is the source A (statement lines 1856-1860). The proof works directly with the characterisation of weak pre-adicness rather than with its definition. It first obtains pre-admissibility of A from the corresponding descent statement for admissibility, so that it remains to show that the closure of a power of an ideal of definition is open (proof lines 1862-1870). Fixing an ideal of definition of A and an exponent, the proof chooses a fundamental system of open ideals of A and passes to the closures of their extensions to B; since B is weakly pre-adic the closure of the power of the extension of the chosen ideal is open, so one of the extended open ideals lies inside the intersection which computes that closure, an identification supplied by the lemma describing closures as intersections of quotients (proof lines 1870-1882). Rewriting that containment modulo each member of the fundamental system, using that every element of the closure agrees with an element of the extension of the chosen ideal modulo that member, gives a containment of the images of the two ideals in the quotient of B; faithful flatness of the maps between the quotients then descends the containment to A, and one reads off that the chosen open ideal lies in the closure of the power of the ideal of definition, which is therefore open (proof lines 1882-1890). The claim is H2: a single descent is carried out, but it requires the reduction to a topological statement, the identification of a closure by an intersection, and a faithfully flat descent of an inclusion of ideals, each displayed with its reason.
